NAMINGRULES — UPDATE v1.1

Preserve established canonical names and expansions unless explicitly
changed. Names are labels; canonical IDs define identity. Prefer real
semantic bridges; avoid forced backronyms. Strong naming has three
layers where useful: FUNCTIONAL — what it means/does. CONCEPTUAL — why
the metaphor/name fits. BEHAVIORAL — how that metaphor informs
interaction.

LITERARY / POETIC USER-FACING NAMING RULE

Where appropriate, user-facing names should favor memorable, evocative,
literary or poetic language over dry administrative or geographic
terminology, provided clarity is preserved.

Pattern: EVOCATIVE TITLE → CLEAR FUNCTIONAL / GEOGRAPHIC / CULTURAL
SUBTITLE → EXPLICIT CONTENT OR CAPABILITY DESCRIPTION.

Internal canonical IDs remain precise, stable and functional. Poetic
naming must never obscure what something does, create identity
ambiguity, or replace technical identifiers.

A name may evoke journeys, landscapes, literature, nature, history,
exploration or human connection without claiming that the metaphor
literally defines the people, culture or geography represented.

DIRECTION, NOT DESTINATION: An inspiration such as “Jasmine Road”
establishes naming character and vocabulary. It does not require literal
reuse or derivative names.

Especially applicable to LINGUA coverage packs, collections, discovery
surfaces and user-facing experiences. Technical components should remain
functional where poetry would reduce clarity.

Example: Jasmine Coast East Africa & the Indian Ocean [visible included
language list]

PACKAGE RULE

Canonical display: [ACRONYM] — [Expanded Functional Meaning] —
v[VERSION]

Root: [ACRONYM]_[Expanded_Name]_v[VERSION]/

Human-readable docs default to TXT. Every package includes README.txt.
MASTER must be self-contained/current where applicable. Do not package
obsolete or contradictory masters as current.
